card.plain_headline: US dollar weakens on cooling inflation

card.what_happened_verbose: The latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for June showed that inflation in the United States eased more than anticipated. This data suggests that the Federal Reserve might not need to raise interest rates as much as previously feared to control rising prices. As a result, the US dollar weakened because lower interest rates generally make a currency less appealing to foreign investors seeking higher returns. This impacts global markets as a weaker dollar can make US exports cheaper and imports more expensive.

card.what_happened: Short-term US government bond yields have surged to multi-year highs due to heightened geopolitical tensions, specifically related to US-Iran missile strikes and a potential crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.
